titles.169: Decem Theses open: Francus vernacular compendium of Annotatio I — subjoined to his polemical tract
titles.170: Decem Theses I: AC exemplar 1530-1540 grew; after correction, unchanged a hundred years
titles.171: Decem Theses II: Two Imperial exemplars — Wittenberg 1531 and augmented 1540/41 to Ferdinand at Naumburg 1561
titles.172: Decem Theses III-IV: One Confession in two exemplars; Formula Concord insert differs in words, not substance
titles.173: Decem Theses V-VI: Either exemplar makes an AC Socius; Estates publicly professed the augmented as the prior
titles.174: Decem Theses VII-VIII: Imperial Acts name neither Variata nor Invariata; oral eating and ubiquity absent — Reformed not excludable
titles.175: Decem Theses IX-X close: Tolerate ubiquitism still; Luther and Melanchthon dissented on Coena yet stayed Socii — so Reformed; Addendum Bajerus

latin.169: Annotationis praecedentis, utpotè paulò prolixioris breve Compendium, jampridem, Decem Thesibus, in Vernacula nostra, ab Excellentissimo quondam hujus Universitatis Doctore & Professore Theologo, B. Gregorio Gregorii Franco, comprehensum, ac Tractatui cuidam suo Polemico, publicis typis exscripto, Subjunctum.
latin.170:
I.
Quanquam Augustanae Confessionis exemplar, An. 1530. primùm exhibitum, ad ann. usque 1540, in quibusdam sensim auctum emendatumque fuerit, ex eo tamen tempore in posteriori correcto exemplari, per centum annos, ne litera quidem immutata est.
latin.171:
II.
Duo interim Exemplaria propriè loquendô ab Electoribus, Principibus & Statibus Imperii agnita & exhibita sunt, inque scriptis Lutheri & Melanchthonis & Actis Imperii reperiunda: Prius Wittenbergae An. 31. impressum; Posterius An. 40. & 41. auctum Caesarique Ferdinando I. unà cum priori, An. 1561. Naumburgô transmissum, cui ad hanc usq; diem nihil additum ademptumque fuit.
latin.172:
III.
Duo illa exemplaria, non duplicem, sed unam eandemq; Confessionem continent, nec posterius à priori, substantialibus fidei articulis, sed solis verbis clariorique explicatione, differt.
IV.
Exemplar Augustanae Confessionis, Formulae Concordiae insertum, in quibusdam quidem verbis, ab eo, quod Wittebergae An. 31. impressum in Tomis Lutheri invenitur, est diversum; in substantialibus tamen plenè cum eodem convenit.
latin.173:
V.
Qui alterutram harum Confessionum recipit, Socius est Augustanae Confessionis, nec religiosa Imperii pace jure excludi potest.
VI.
Electores, Principes, ac Status Imperii, adauctam Confessionem aequè ac priorem, publice professi sunt.
latin.174:
VII.
Nec Recessus, nec Acta Edictave Imperii, vel variatae, vel invariatae Augustanae Confessionis (Sub bisputa Denominationibus) mentionem ullam faciunt.
VIII.
Recens quorundam Evangelicorum, Bergensi Formulae addictorum doctrina, de orali manducatione, & ubiquitate Corporis Christi, nec in priori, nec auctiori Confessione, multò minùs in ejusdem Repetitione & Corpore Doctrinae Philippi reperitur; Unde nec Reformati Augustanae Confessionis Socii, ob haec duo dogmata negata, pace Imperii excludi possunt.
latin.175:
IX.
Utut Ubiquitismus, & quicquid ei annexum est, ingens error sit, quoniam tamen per actum quendam solennem, in Generali quadam aut Nationali Synodo, nondum improbatus est, propugnatores quoque ejus adeò diversimodè de eo loquuntur, ut quid propriè statuant, intelligi vix queat, aestimandum est, tolerari adhuc, & approbantes istum, nihilo secius Augustanae Confessionis Sociis annumerandos esse.
X.
Quemadmodum & D. Lutherus, & M. Phil. Melanchthon, Augustanae Confessionis Socii fuêre, tales ab omnibus habiti, eique ad finem usque viae ex intimo corde addicti permansêre, licèt de modo exhibitionis Corporis Christi in S. Coena, dissenserint; Ita Reformati aequè ac Lutherani Socii Augustanae Confessionis permanent, quamvis in eodem, & aliis quibusdam quaestionibus scholasticis, non penitus inter se conveniant.
Addendum & emendandum:
Pag. 13. lin. 5. Pro: Christianum Pontanum, lege: Christianum Bajerum, postquam SERENISSIMUS ELECTOR ab IMPERATORE CAROLO V. precibus impetrasset, ut Augustana Confessio, in Germania inq Augusta Vindelicorum Civitate, etiam Germanico Idiomate prelegeretur. Vid. Clar. Pipping/ in der Einleitung zu den Symbol. Schrifften Lutherischer Kirchen.

pass_a.169: A brief Compendium of the preceding Annotation, as being a little more prolix, long since comprehended in Ten Theses, in our Vernacular, by the most Excellent sometime Doctor and Theological Professor of this University, B. Gregorius Gregorii Francus, and Subjoined to a certain Polemical Tract of his, written out in public types.
pass_a.170: I. Although the exemplar of the Augsburg Confession, first exhibited in the Year 1530, was by degrees in certain things increased and emended up to the year 1540, yet from that time in the later corrected exemplar, through a hundred years, not even a letter has been changed.
pass_a.171: II. Meanwhile two Exemplars, properly speaking, have been acknowledged and exhibited by the Electors, Princes, and Estates of the Empire, and are to be found in the writings of Luther and Melanchthon and in the Acts of the Empire: the Earlier printed at Wittenberg in the Year 31; the Later augmented in the Years 40 and 41 and transmitted to Emperor Ferdinand I together with the earlier one at Naumburg in the Year 1561, to which up to this very day nothing has been added or taken away.
pass_a.172: III. Those two exemplars contain not a twofold, but one and the same Confession, nor does the later differ from the earlier in the substantial articles of faith, but only in words and in a clearer explanation. IV. The exemplar of the Augsburg Confession inserted into the Formula of Concord is indeed in certain words diverse from that which, printed at Wittenberg in the Year 31, is found in Luther's Tomes; yet in substantial matters it fully agrees with the same.
pass_a.173: V. Whoever receives either of these Confessions is an Associate of the Augsburg Confession, and cannot by right be excluded from the Religious Peace of the Empire. VI. The Electors, Princes, and Estates of the Empire have publicly professed the augmented Confession equally with the earlier one.
pass_a.174: VII. Neither the Recesses, nor the Acts or Edicts of the Empire, make any mention either of the Variata or of the Invariata Augsburg Confession (under these disputed Denominations). VIII. The recent doctrine of certain Evangelicals devoted to the Bergen Formula, concerning oral manducation and the ubiquity of Christ's Body, is found neither in the earlier nor in the more augmented Confession, much less in the same's Repetition and in Philip's Body of Doctrine; Whence neither can the Reformed Associates of the Augsburg Confession, on account of these two dogmas denied, be excluded from the Peace of the Empire.
pass_a.175: IX. Even though Ubiquitism, and whatever is annexed to it, be a huge error, yet because it has not yet been disapproved by any solemn act in some General or National Synod, and its champions also speak of it in modes so diverse that what they properly hold can scarcely be understood, it is to be judged that it is still to be tolerated, and that those approving it are nonetheless to be numbered among the Associates of the Augsburg Confession. X. Just as both D. Luther and M. Phil. Melanchthon were Associates of the Augsburg Confession, held as such by all, and remained devoted to it from the inmost heart to the end of the way, although they dissented concerning the mode of exhibition of Christ's Body in the Holy Supper; So the Reformed equally with the Lutherans remain Associates of the Augsburg Confession, although in that same matter, and in certain other scholastic questions, they do not entirely agree among themselves. Addendum and thing to be emended: Page 13, line 5. For: Christianum Pontanum, read: Christianum Bajerum, after the Most Serene Elector had by prayers obtained from Emperor Charles V that the Augsburg Confession, in Germany and in the City of Augsburg, should also be read aloud in the German Idiom. See Clar. Pipping in the Einleitung zu den Symbol. Schrifften Lutherischer Kirchen.

169: Here is a short compendium of the preceding Annotation — which ran a little long — cast long ago into Ten Theses in our vernacular by the late excellent doctor and theology professor of this University, B. Gregorius Gregorii Francus, and printed as an appendix to one of his polemical tracts.
170: I. Though the Augsburg Confession text first shown in 1530 was, in places, gradually enlarged and corrected through 1540, from that time the later corrected exemplar has not changed so much as a letter for a hundred years.
171: II. Properly speaking, two exemplars have been acknowledged and presented by the Electors, Princes, and Imperial Estates, and they stand in Luther's and Melanchthon's writings and in the Imperial Acts.

The earlier was printed at Wittenberg in 1531; the later, enlarged in 1540 and 1541, was sent with the earlier one to Emperor Ferdinand I at Naumburg in 1561 — and to this day nothing has been added to it or taken from it.
172: III. Those two exemplars are not two confessions, but one and the same: the later differs from the earlier not in the substance of the faith's articles, but only in wording and clearer explanation.
IV. The Augsburg Confession text slotted into the Formula of Concord does differ in some words from the 1531 Wittenberg printing in Luther's volumes; in substance, though, it fully matches that text.
173: V. Anyone who receives either of these Confessions is an associate of the Augsburg Confession, and cannot lawfully be shut out of the Empire's Religious Peace.
VI. Electors, Princes, and Imperial Estates have publicly professed the enlarged Confession no less than the earlier one.
174: VII. Neither Imperial Recesses nor Acts or Edicts ever mention a Variata or Invariata Augsburg Confession under those contested labels.

VIII. The recent teaching of certain Evangelicals bound to the Bergen Formula — oral eating and the ubiquity of Christ's body — is in neither the earlier nor the enlarged Confession, and still less in the Repetitio or in Philip's Corpus Doctrinae.
So the Reformed, as associates of the Augsburg Confession, cannot be shut out of the Imperial Peace for denying those two dogmas.
175: IX. Ubiquitism and whatever hangs on it may be a huge error; still, no solemn act of a general or national synod has yet condemned it, and its defenders talk about it in such different ways that one can hardly tell what they actually hold.
So it should still be tolerated, and those who approve it should nonetheless be counted among the associates of the Augsburg Confession.

X. Luther and Melanchthon were associates of the Augsburg Confession, held as such by everyone, and stayed heart-devoted to it to the end of their course, even though they disagreed on how Christ's body is exhibited in the Holy Supper.
In the same way the Reformed, no less than the Lutherans, remain associates of the Augsburg Confession, even when they do not fully agree on that point and on certain other school questions.

Addendum and correction: p. 13, line 5 — for Christianum Pontanum read Christianum Bajerum, after the Most Serene Elector obtained by petition from Emperor Charles V that the Augsburg Confession should also be read aloud in German in Germany and in the city of Augsburg. See Clar. Pipping, Einleitung zu den Symbol. Schrifften Lutherischer Kirchen.
